I have been working this land for 26 years, and at 46 I know what the soil in Quzhou County will give me. With 7 mu total and four people in my household—some of us working off-farm when the busy season is over—I need a plan that balances grain for eating and cotton for cash without taking more labor than we have.

I will put **5 mu into my wheat-maize rotation** and keep **2 mu for cotton**. The wheat-maize double crop is the backbone of our farm; it is reliable and the government supports it. The 2 mu of cotton gives us better money per mu, but it needs hand-picking and many pesticide sprays, so I cannot expand it beyond what my family can manage.

For the **winter wheat on 5 mu**, I will sow an improved variety in autumn—the same kind my neighbors plant. Before sowing I will do rotary tillage to break up the stubble and level the field. Wheat is hungry, so I will put down about 35 kg of nitrogen per mu, 18 kg of phosphorus, and 8 kg of potassium. Because I have a well, I will irrigate three times: once at green-up in spring, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I will spray pesticides four times to keep aphids and rust away. I expect around 1000 kg per mu if the weather holds.

Right after wheat harvest in early June, I will plant **hybrid maize on the same 5 mu**. Here we use no-tillage; there is no time to plough between crops, and the maize seeds go straight into the wheat stubble. Maize needs roughly 22 kg nitrogen, 22 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. Summer brings some rain, so two irrigations—at tasseling and grain filling—are enough. Four pesticide applications will handle corn borers and weeds. I expect about 1100 kg per mu.

For my **2 mu of cotton**, I will rotary till in April and plant a good improved variety. Cotton is a cash crop but it is thirsty for chemicals. I will apply about 18 kg nitrogen, 15 kg phosphorus, and 15 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice during the hot months and spray pesticides about 16 times through the season to control bollworms and mites—that is simply what cotton demands in this area. I expect roughly 550 kg of seed cotton per mu.

This is my plan. It keeps us fed, uses our well water wisely, and brings in cash without overloading the family.
